home.heroLede: Operator-grade guides, considered tours, and a concierge that actually listens. Cairo-based, founder-led, with three decades of Egyptian travel experience.
home.standfirstLine1: Most travel sites treat Egypt as a checklist of monuments.
home.standfirstLine2: We treat it as a country with eighty million people, four major dialects, and several thousand years of opinions about itself.
home.standfirstAccent: The difference shows up in the details.

hieroglyphs.heading: Your Name in Hieroglyphs
hieroglyphs.subheading: Type any name and see it written in the phonetic alphabet of ancient Egyptian scribes.
hieroglyphs.banner: Hieroglyphs can be read right-to-left, left-to-right, or top-to-bottom — direction depends on which way the bird and animal glyphs face.
hieroglyphs.emptyState: Start typing to see your name appear.
hieroglyphs.cartoucheToggle: Wrap in a cartouche (the royal frame)
hieroglyphs.disclaimer: This is a phonetic transliteration — a fun, modern approximation. Ancient scribes used hieroglyphs symbolically and grammatically; names were typically written within a cartouche (oval frame) reserved for royalty. Letters such as C/K, E/I, F/V, and O/U/W share glyphs because ancient Egyptian didn't distinguish those sounds the way modern English does.
hieroglyphs.ctaPrompt: Curious how these signs were used by the people who carved them?
hieroglyphs.metaDescription: Translate any name into Egyptian hieroglyphs using the phonetic alphabet of the ancient scribes. Free, instant, shareable — wrap your name in a royal cartouche.

distances.subheading: Searchable table of 104 routes across 25 cities. Toggle km/mi, set your average driving speed, and the drive times recalculate live.
distances.disclaimer: Distances are road distances between city centers. Drive times are estimates based on your selected average speed; actual times vary with traffic, weather, fuel stops, and security checkpoints. For Sinai and Eastern Desert routes, plan extra time for checkpoints.
